source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 68: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and scope: define the production model revision, tokenizer, prompt and output distributions, context-length distribution, sampling/decoding settings, serving engine and version, quantization algorithm, weight bit-width/group size/scales, calibration data, hardware, software stack, batch/concurrency policy, and cost accounting period before testing. Compare an unquantized reference and the weight-only candidate with identical model weights apart from quantization, prompts, seeds, stopping rules, request mix, and service-level targets. Report measured facts with units; do not treat nominal bits per weight as total serving memory or assume every kernel supports the format.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at a fixed quality and tail-latency target, weight-only quantization reduces total cost per accepted output token by reducing resident weight memory enough to improve feasible replica packing or throughput, without unacceptable quality or failure regressions. It is falsified if the candidate misses quality/SLO gates, has unsupported or fallback kernels, increases TTFT/TPOT or failure rate enough to offset packing gains, or produces no statistically supported cost reduction. A secondary hypothesis is that any benefit is workload- and batch-dependent; reject it only after testing the prespecified workload strata rather than relying on one average.

Controlled experiment: freeze the reference and candidate artifacts, use the same hardware pool, engine configuration, tokenizer, prompt set, calibration split, warmup procedure, and randomized request trace. First verify numerical output correctness on a held-out task suite, including long contexts, rare tokens, structured output, and adversarial/error cases. Measure quality separately by task and aggregate with confidence intervals; record exact-match/pass rate, calibrated or reference-scored metrics where applicable, refusals, malformed outputs, and unacceptable regressions. Run repeated randomized trials at prespecified concurrency and offered-load levels, with enough warmup to reach steady state. Measure TTFT and TPOT in milliseconds, throughput in accepted output tokens/s and requests/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, queueing, timeouts, OOMs, retries, and error rate. Record peak and steady-state GPU memory in GiB, resident weights, KV cache, workspace, fragmentation, utilization, power, replica count, and whether kernels are native or fallback. Compute cost from a declared formula including accelerator time, host time, power or rental price, replicas, and failed/retried work; report uncertainty and paired confidence intervals for deltas.

Fairness and confounders: match quality data and decoding exactly; separate quantization calibration data from evaluation data and prevent leakage. Stratify by prompt length, output length, task, concurrency, and batch shape. Control run order, thermal state, clocking, background load, autoscaling, cache state, driver/runtime versions, tensor-parallel placement, and admission limits. Do not claim savings from a larger batch or different SLO unless that policy is part of the declared deployment comparison. Test each supported kernel path explicitly; a silent dequantization or fallback is a different system and must be reported.

Decision and rollback: keep the candidate only if it passes all predeclared quality, correctness, safety, error-rate, and p99 SLO gates and its paired cost reduction has a confidence interval excluding the required minimum benefit. Otherwise reject it for that workload or rewrite the deployment plan; do not average away a critical slice failure. Canary behind an explicit feature flag, cap traffic, retain the reference artifact, monitor quality proxies, TTFT/TPOT, p99, OOMs, errors, memory, and cost, and roll back immediately on a gate breach. Evidence is provisional until artifacts, traces, repeated trial data, confidence-interval calculations, and the exact cost model are archived and independently reproducible.
risks: quality degradation hidden by aggregate scores
kernel fallback or memory overhead masking nominal quantization savings
workload, thermal, batching, and cost-model confounding
calibration/evaluation leakage or unsupported output formats
evidence_required: frozen artifact and software manifest
held-out per-task quality and correctness results
repeated paired latency/throughput/memory trials with units and confidence intervals
kernel support and fallback audit
declared cost model and canary/rollback telemetry
